_about: The bag clue lines and Sir Irwin's sharing prompts (docs/handoff-2026-10-23.md sections 9.1 to 9.3 and 15.4; docs/sensory-bags.md section 5). Open content: Jon may read and rewrite any line. Only the game's fill on the night is sealed: which clue word goes in each blank. Read by functions/lib/bagclues.js. In a line, ___ is the clue word the game fills from the packing (a word that sits in two or three of the bags in play, never one). [sense] is the sense as a noun (smell, sound, touch, taste, sight); [sense:verb] as a verb (smell, hear, touch, taste, see); [sense:organ] as the part that notices (nose, ear, fingers, tongue, eye). Each cat has five lines, one per rung of its ladder (affection 1 to 5). Rungs 1 and 2 give no clue word, so every visit reads about the same length.

act2._about: Act 2, at each cat's room, about the Murderer. The rung is the cat's affection for the guest at the scan. Salem is filled with a WRONG word at rungs 1 to 3, a coin flip at 4, the right one at 5; his wording never changes, so nobody can tell. Boo speaks only at 4 or above in Act 2.
granolia: Oh! The bag. I saw a bag. Someone's bag. It was... a bag. I'm sorry, I licked a book and now it's all gone.
The Murderer's bag! I sniffed it. Or heard it. Or... one of those. There was definitely a something.
There's something in the Murderer's bag that you'd only notice if you [sense:verb] it. I noticed. Then I forgot.
Something in the Murderer's bag was ___. Or near enough. Or I'm thinking of a different bag. No. I'm fairly sure. Mostly.
I remember this one! Something in the Murderer's bag is ___. Write that down before I lose it again.
zimothy: I have a note on the Murderer's bag. It is not free.
The Murderer's bag contains something of interest to the [sense:organ]. That is all my fee covers.
For the record: an item in the Murderer's bag is best examined by [sense]. Further particulars cost extra.
My file says the Murderer's bag holds something one might call ___. I will not swear to the wording.
My file is clear. The Murderer's bag holds something ___. Filed, witnessed, and billed.
boo: Boo looks you up and down. She says nothing about any bag.
Ew. Do I know you? No. Then I don't know anything about anybody's bag.
I'm off duty, darling. Ask me again when we're friends.
The Murderer's bag holds something ___. I'd know. I knocked it off a table.
salem: Off my lawn. Fine. The Murderer's bag? Something ___ in it. Now git.
Saw the Murderer's bag go by. Something ___. Don't ask me twice.
Forty years on these grounds. The Murderer's bag had something ___ in it. I'd swear to it.
The Murderer's bag. Something ___. Or the other thing. One of the two.
You're all right, you are. The Murderer's bag holds something ___. Straight up, no lawn jokes.

act4._about: Act 4, with each game room's reward, about the Ghost (the one who cried out; no line ever says a name). The rung is the group's average affection with that cat. Granolia's lead-in comes first at every rung. Salem gives a word at every rung: wrong at 1 to 3, a coin flip at 4, right at 5. Boo speaks to every group in Act 4.

leadIn.granolia: Oh! Also! Before I forget, and I will:

granolia: Someone shouted for help. I was reading. Was it a book? No. A person. I think.
When the shout came, there was a... a [sense] thing. Near them. I forget the rest.
The one who shouted had something you'd have to [sense:verb] to know about. I noticed. Then the lights went out.
The one who shouted had something ___ with them. Or near them. Or I'm mixing up chapters.
The one who shouted had something ___ with them. I'm sure. I wrote it in the margin.
zimothy: A cry for help was heard. My notes on it are not free.
The party who cried out carried something for the [sense:organ]. My fee covers no more.
For the record: whoever cried out had something best examined by [sense].
My file says the deceased had something one might call ___ about them. No warranty.
My file is clear. The victim carried something ___. Filed, witnessed, billed.
salem: Heard the yelp from the lawn. Whoever it was had something ___ on 'em. Forty years, never wrong.
That yelp. Something ___ went with it. I'd stake the hedges on it.
Whoever hollered had something ___ about 'em. Mark it down.
The yelp? Something ___ went with it. Or didn't. Fifty-fifty, like my knees.
Straight up, no lawn jokes: whoever yelped had something ___ on 'em.
boo: Ugh. Fine. Whoever screamed had something... [sense]-ish about them. Don't make me say more.
Ew. Do I know you? No. But the one who screamed had something for the [sense:organ]. There.
The scream. Something ___-ish. Five words, darling. I'm done.
The one who screamed? Something ___ about them. Dreadful, really.
Darling, whoever screamed carried something ___. I'd know. I was judging them at the time.

prompts._about: Sir Irwin's sharing prompts on the Parlour TV during the Act 2 cat visits and in Act 4 (sections 9.3 and 15.4). One at a time, a new one every everyMinutes, random order, no repeat until all of them have shown. A prompt never contains a clue word (check L08); prompts 13 to 16 name a tag or a shape (spooky, round, a chew, a no-no). The guest chooses what to share; nothing from the Parlour is recorded.
lines: Show someone something from your bag that makes a sound. I'll be listening. I'm always listening.
Let a friend smell something from your bag. Nothing says friendship like sniffing.
Pass around something from your bag that's nice to touch. Nicer than me? Impossible. Try anyway.
Show someone the best-looking thing in your bag. Ooh. Look at it.
Got a snack in there? Show it. Don't eat it. Don't give it to me. Okay, give it to me.
Let someone feel something from your bag with their eyes closed. Don't tell them what it is.
Find someone who hasn't seen inside your bag yet. Say hi. Share one thing. Sniffing optional.
Show someone something you could smell from across the room. I could smell it from the garden.
Make a sound with something from your bag. Then do it again. I liked it.
Show someone the smallest thing in your bag. I'm not allowed to have small things.
Share something from your bag that's good to taste. Then explain to me why dogs can't have it.
Share whatever you like. I trust you. I trust everyone. It's a problem.
Anything round in your bag? Roll it to a friend. Not to me. I will chase it. I can't help it.
Show someone the thing in your bag I'd most like to chew. Then keep it away from me. Far away.
Got something a dog shouldn't eat? Show it from a safe distance. I'm faster than I look.
Got something spooky in your bag? Show a friend. I'll be over here, being very brave.
